fix(render): a client timeout, on the connect or after it, kicks nothing (candybar-launch-q7o7.6wi)

A dead daemon never times out: a missing socket is ENOENT and an unbound one
ECONNREFUSED, both immediate. A timeout therefore means a live listener, and a
kick's candidate loses the bind to it (socket-lease arbitration). Both runtimes
now classify the client's own connect/deadline timeouts as busy, and the
unreachable-by-construction transient 'timeout' cause is removed.

fix(render): a render the daemon answers TIMEOUT kicks nothing (candybar-launch-q7o7.g6w) (#574)

* fix(render): a render the daemon answers TIMEOUT kicks nothing, in both runtimes (candybar-launch-q7o7.g6w)

The daemon's own TIMEOUT proves it is up; each kick spawned a candidate
that lost the bind to it. planOutcome stops kicking on busy and the Rust
client gets a Busy variant that emits the stale frame without a kick.

* docs(render): the Timeout cause is the client's own clock, and the Busy comments say what they mean (candybar-launch-q7o7.g6w)

* docs(protocol): TIMEOUT is busy, not a respawn-curable transient (candybar-launch-q7o7.g6w)
